# Rotated text at fractional table origins

Original controls generated by `tools/cell_text_direction_origin_phase_fixture.py`
from the original repeated-glyph fixture. Eight pages retain identical Arial
10pt runs, automatic paragraph spacing, exact row height, cell widths and
margins. Only table indentation varies: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 and 20 twips.
Explicit zero indentation differs from absent indentation in the base fixture;
compare the eight pages with each other, not their absolute origin with the base.

The native reference PDF contains nonmonotonic top-to-bottom (`tbRl`) baseline
coordinates. Increasing indentation from zero to one twip moves the third
baseline from 237.05pt to 236.93pt: left by 0.12pt despite the table moving right
by 0.05pt. Other lines move differently. Bottom-to-top (`btLr`) coordinates
remain monotonic across all offsets. Font identity and PDF size remain ArialMT
and 9.96pt for every rotated run. This rules out a constant baseline correction
or a changed font/line-height metric as an explanation of the complete result.
It suggests a rotation/export coordinate-quantization effect; its exact
algorithm is not established. No renderer change or relaxed tolerance follows.

## Paired native drawing records — September 29, 2026

The sixteen `native-{page,table}-N.emf` files capture each original table both
alone and together with its preceding page label through the reference application's
`Range.EnhMetaFileBits`. These are original text/drawing records, not embedded
font binaries. The page-range and table-range horizontal origins agree exactly
for all 96 rotated labels. This guards against an extraction-dependent X shift;
it does not certify live-screen rasterization or all reference range extraction.

`record_rotated_phase_metafiles.py` validates left/baseline alignment, zero
origins, constant extents, absence of viewport/world transforms, both rotation
angles, Arial identity and the unchanged glyph advances before converting the
horizontal frame scale. Each logical unit is 0.12pt. The source, PDF, cases,
earlier PDF reference and all native captures are bound in `native-reference.json`.

The third tbRl baseline moves from logical X 1375 to 1374 when indentation
increases by one twip, while the first baseline moves right. Within-direction
baseline increments agree with PDF increments within 0.01pt across all eight
offsets. The nonmonotonic behavior therefore precedes PDF serialization: it is
present in native GDI records too. The earlier PDF-only hypothesis is insufficient.
Absolute PDF/EMF coordinates remain distinct references; no fitted translation
or font-specific offset is applied. The existing strict renderer failures remain.

The separate reference range API probe again returns positions on a 0.75pt grid,
as in the earlier `../native-text` controls. It cannot establish the finer
rounding rule. Do not repeat that route as a precise baseline oracle. A useful
next control must distinguish the stages of native rotated-origin calculation,
with multiple fonts/line advances and translations, before changing layout.

Reproduce after opening this source in the reference application with the reference-opening helper:

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/capture-rotated-phase-metafiles.ps1 -SourceFullPath "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/origin-phase/control.docx" -OutputDirectory "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/origin-phase"
python tools/record_rotated_phase_metafiles.py
python tests/rotated_phase_metafile_test.py
```

The recorder is intentionally bounded to this original control. It is not a
general EMF renderer, and rejects unhandled mapping/alignment rather than
assuming those records have no effect. Review regenerated reference differences.

Relevant OOXML properties are §17.4.72 (`textDirection`), §17.4.50 (`tblInd`),
and §17.3.1.33 (`spacing`). The evidence concerns native PDF coordinates, not
the reference application's on-screen pixel rendering. No normative requirement for these numerical
rounding steps is claimed.

The browser opens all eight pages editable and passes exact no-edit package
preservation, insertion, unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and edited
reopening. The source and three browser exports pass XML schema validation.
Existing `origins` and `height` layout tests retain their exact expected
failures. No corpus completion count changes.

Reproduce with the generator, export `control.docx` using
`tools/export-reference.ps1`, then run
`tools/record_cell_text_direction_origin_phase.py`. The recorder checks all
96 rotated runs and records source/PDF hashes. No font files are bundled.
